formula.demand: (sum w_i*pct_i + 50*0.15) / (sum w_i + 0.15) over available inputs; null if sum w_i < 0.1
formula.cost: 100 - percentile(ACS median home value) [x0.75] + 100 - percentile(FHFA trend) [x0.25], re-weighted if trend missing
formula.score: score = demand * (0.6 + 0.4 * cost/100) (demand after credibility shrinkage); score_raw uses demand_raw
formula.credibility: demand = 50 + w*(demand_raw-50), w = n/(n+4.0), n = max(0, log10(households)-2)^2
formula.market_depth: percentile of mean(pct(households), mean pct of absolute visitor-volume inputs)
formula.intensity_cap: tourism_intensity weight x acc_emp/200 when acc_emp < 200
formula.housing: weighted mean of input percentiles (sign -1 inputs inverted), re-weighted over available inputs

labels.federal_land_visits: Federal land (NPS/USFS/BLM/USACE/FWS) recreation visits in county

MN.value: No state preemption of STR rules found; cities license STRs (Minneapolis licence, Saint Paul Ch. 379). State and local taxes apply and facilitating platforms collect.

TX.value: No state STR preemption statute found. Zaatari v. City of Austin (Tex. App.-Austin, Nov 27, 2019, No. 03-17-00812-CV) partly struck Austin's STR rules; review denied Jun 11, 2021. Dallas STR zoning ban is before the Texas Supreme Court (No. 25-0748).

CO.value: No statewide STR preemption found; HB23-1287 (signed 2023) instead concerns county regulation of STRs. Home-rule cities such as Denver and Boulder license STRs themselves.

OH.value: No statewide STR preemption enacted. HB 563 (134th GA, 2022) was reported from committee but never passed; later bills not checked.

OK.value: None found: the Title 11 (municipal) index has no STR section; cities such as Tulsa license STRs directly.

MO.value: No state STR preemption law: an official statute search for 'short-term rental' returns only an unrelated tax section (RSMo 137.018). Pending bills not checked.

AL.value: No STR preemption found; cities regulate via zoning and business licences. State lodging tax (Ala. Code 40-26-1) covers stays under 180 days: 5% in Madison and other mountain-lakes counties, 4% elsewhere. Platform collection not confirmed.

AZ.value: Cities and counties may not ban STRs or regulate them by classification, use or occupancy. They may require a permit (max $250, decision in 7 business days), emergency contact, neighbour notice, licence number on ads, $500,000 insurance, owner residence only for post-9/14/2024 ADUs; fines $500-$3,500 and suspensions up to 12 months.

legal_scope.city: status from rules.json for the listed cities (inside city limits only)
legal_scope.state: no city rules checked; state STR-preemption note in meta.state_preemption[st]
legal_scope.null: local and state STR rules not checked

caveats: Estimate from aggregate public data; no booking or occupancy data is used. No nightly rates, ADR, RevPAR or occupancy are estimated: we have no permanently free, commercial-use public source for them.
Demand is a relative percentile index across US counties (0-100), not a forecast of bookings or income.
Inputs missing for a county are dropped and the remaining weights re-normalised; 'coverage' = share of total weight present.
Legal status is never folded into the score; a county with a ban can still score high on demand. Read 'legal' first.
Legal entries cover only the 12 cities in rules.json (inside city limits) plus state-preemption notes; everything else is 'unknown'.
Cost uses ACS 5-year median home value (lags the market by 2-3 years); FHFA trend used only if a trend column exists.
Housing demand (counties[fips].housing) is a separate 0-100 index for buying / long-term renting; it does not feed the STR score.
sources: rules.json (project legal research; verified flags per field)
